     "content": "The show on the **HŽV Siempre** channel is opened by host **Marjan (Siempre)** in a distinctly celebratory mood, greeting his interlocutors **Vinko Dubravica** and **Frane**. The occasion for great joy and toasting is **Hajduk's** victory in the derby against **Dinamo**, which allows the whole crew to finally host the show with pleasure and without bitterness. Although it is a rainy Saturday at 9 PM, Marjan metaphorically points out that for the entire Hajduk faithful, the sun is shining outside and the little birds are singing, despite the fact that due to spending the whole day in the rain, he is already starting to catch a slight fever.\n\nLooking ahead to the upcoming schedule, Marjan emphasizes that the upcoming league match on Sunday against **Varaždin**, whom they need to pay back for an earlier slip-up, is far more important to him than the European clash with **Ajax** on Thursday. Speaking about the conditions at the **Poljud** stadium itself, the host describes how the rain did not ruin the experience for the fans at all, even though it caused serious problems in the stands. Located in the east stand, Marjan witnesses how water leaked directly through the worn-out roof panels, forcing spectators to squeeze together and retreat upwards, onto the stairs and into the aisles. On the other hand, in the north stand, the fans had nowhere to run from the precipitation, so they simply stripped to the waist and continued cheering in a top-notch atmosphere.",

     "content": "Analyzing the first impressions from the pitch, **Vinko Dubravica** recalls a comment from the pre-match Hajduk podcasts in which someone, due to the forecast of all-day rain and mud, expressed regret that Hajduk today does not have a player like **Ivan Gudelj**. The team breathed as one, tracked back for every lost ball, and went into every duel with maximum firmness.\n\nAs the match progressed towards the end, the playing conditions became on the verge of regularity and turned into real water polo, so Marjan jokingly mentions a viewer's comment that a water polo center forward should have been subbed into the game. The host points out that it is a true miracle that no one was seriously injured on such a pitch, because it was impossible to predict whether the ball would pass through or suddenly stop in a huge puddle of water. As the most vivid example of such madness on the pitch, Marjan singles out a situation right before the end of the match when a player tried to carry the ball out, but it got stuck in deep water, after which he realized that the only solution was to lift it into the air, and he managed to juggle it on his foot five times in a row to carry it forward.",

Vinko adds that Hajduk has finally overcome its old ailment of always being a step too short; this time the Split players were half a step faster on every ball. With a dose of irony, Vinko also thanks the Scottish center-back in Dinamo's ranks, calling him a true gentleman who generously helped the hosts with the goals, and nearly scored another own goal as well.\n\nThe celebratory atmosphere in the studio is further warmed up by numerous donations and messages from viewers.      "screenshot_description": "Frane and Vinko Dubravica talk about the unity in the stands and the catastrophic state of the infrastructure at Poljud",
     "content": "Speaking about the atmosphere in the city and at the stadium itself, **Frane** points out that this was one of the craziest derbies he has witnessed, but without the usual pre-match euphoria. What particularly delighted him is the fact that in the stands, not even in the proverbially critical east stand, was there any grumbling, cursing, or insulting of their own players. The entire **Poljud** – north, east, west, and southeast – breathed as one body, and people genuinely enjoyed themselves despite the weather conditions. **Vinko Dubravica** follows up with a sharp criticism of the infrastructure, pointing out that he would like all the politicians and those who decide on new stadiums and reconstructions to come to a match like this at Poljud. He invites them to sit in row fifty-something while swimming in water, with electrical installations and live current running around them.\n\n**Marjan (Siempre)** completely agrees with Frane's observation about the absence of euphoria, considering it a sign of maturity and rationality among the fanbase this season. He emphasizes that this victory over **Dinamo** will mean absolutely nothing if they lose or draw against **Varaždin** in the next round. The host openly admits that the upcoming European clash with **Ajax** is not even on the back of his mind and that Varaždin is ten times more important to him, because winning the championship after so many dry years is the only key that will finally remove all the heavy shackles from Hajduk's hands and feet.",

     "content": "The topic of conversation shifts to the refereeing of **Igor Pajač**, which **Frane** without hesitation calls the absolute bottom of the barrel. The first disputed situation they analyze is the offensive foul called on Dinamo's goalkeeper **Kotarski**, where **Šutić** was in the duel. **Vinko Dubravica** and **Marjan (Siempre)** point out that from multiple camera angles they did not see any contact for a foul at all, but rather a clean rounding and taking of the ball, while some media outlets are even coming out with insane claims that the Hajduk player should have received a yellow card for obstructing the goalkeeper. Even greater anger in the studio is caused by the criteria for handing out cards, with a special emphasis on **Kačavenda**. The interlocutors agree that due to a series of rough fouls and pulling on the wing, the Dinamo player should not have seen the second half on the pitch at all, because Pajač failed to show him two clear yellow cards in the first half.\n\nTo prove referee Pajač's double standards, Marjan draws a direct parallel with the match in **Osijek**, where the same referee sent off Hajduk's **Brajković** in the first half due to two yellow cards. The host claims that just one of Kačavenda's tackles today was twice as harsh as the fouls for which Brajković was sent to the dressing room back then. Vinko adds another example of inconsistent criteria: he recalls how **Livaja** received a red, that is, a second yellow card for kicking the ball away just a quarter of a second after the referee's whistle, whereas in this derby, in a similar situation, the ball was booted a good five seconds after play was stopped without any sanction. They also mention the uncalled red card for **Beljo** for elbowing at the very beginning of the match.\n\nThe interlocutors then reflect on the media treatment of the derby and the comments of former referee **Bruno Marić**. Marjan sharply attacks *Sportske novosti* and other media outlets that are trying to diminish Hajduk's victory with headlines about \"rolling in the mud\" and water polo, convinced that had Dinamo won, they would be writing about a \"magnificent derby\". Precisely out of that spite, Marjan titled the show itself *Hajduk's Magnificent Victory*. To Frane's question of who even gives media space to Bruno Marić to analyze the refereeing and come to Pajač's defense, Marjan without mincing words concludes that space can only be given to such a person by those who are the same as him, reminding of decades of refereeing injustices to the detriment of the Split club.",

     "content": "Before moving on to individual player ratings, **Frane** opens the question of the marathon stoppage time, referring to an observation by a **Dinamo** fan from the **Balkan Deda** channel.      "content": "The analysis of the flank positions brings a handful of praise, first and foremost for **Hrgović**. Although he had one clumsy clearance for a corner in the first half, the interlocutors agree that he played an excellent match. Vinko Dubravica and Marjan particularly highlight his two top-notch crosses: the first sharp delivery that hit the Dinamo defender for an own goal and the equalizer, and the second, millimeter-precise cross for Šego during Hajduk's second goal, which was practically a pre-assist.\n\nFrane notices an incredible transformation in the young full-back in a short time, pointing out how well he understands and complements Šotiček on the left side, just as he cooperated well with Rebić earlier. Marjan explains that Hrgović's football talent was never in question, but exclusively his head and psychological pressure. Now he has obviously matured: he no longer spreads his arms, does not shake from stress at every touch, and plays without fear, which immediately brings a completely different dimension to his game.\n\nOn the right side, **Kapanadze** is rated as exceptionally decent, combative, and reliable. Frane compares him in consistency to Jarni — not necessarily in playing style, but in the sense that a fan always knows he will get the maximum from him and that he will never play below a solid level.
